title: Soils, Rocks and Minerals
seo_title: Year 3 Science: Soils, Rocks and Minerals Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Compare the observable properties of soils, rocks and minerals and justify their use for particular purposes (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 3 science worksheets on soils, rocks and minerals: sandstone, granite and basalt, Australian minerals such as iron ore, gold and opal, and sandy and clay soils. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: We choose rocks, minerals and soils for their properties.
body_html:
How to think about it

Rocks are made of minerals, and soil is made from broken-down rock mixed with humus, water, air and living things.

  • Rocks differ in colour, grain size, hardness and how much water they let through.
  • Australia mines many minerals: iron ore for steel, bauxite for aluminium, gold, copper, lithium and opal.
  • Sandy soil drains fast; clay soil holds water. Loam, a mix, is best for most plants.
Example

Which soil drains water fastest?

sand has big grains

there are big gaps between them

Answer: sandy soil

Example

Iron ore is used to make…

iron ore is heated in a furnace

Answer: steel

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up rocks and minerals (rocks are made of minerals).
  • Thinking soil has nothing living in it.
  • Thinking all rocks are hard and heavy (pumice floats).

faq.q: What is the difference between a rock and a mineral?
faq.a: A mineral is a natural solid with the same make-up all through it, such as quartz. A rock is made of one or more minerals.
Soil is made of tiny pieces of rock, humus (rotted plants and animals), water, air and living things such as worms and bacteria.
Uluru is sandstone that contains iron minerals. The iron has rusted, which makes the rock look red.
